title: Environment variables and standard error
summary: A case-insensitive search developed test-first, reading the IGNORE_CASE environment variable, standard output versus standard error, eprintln!, and redirecting output. Ends with the whole minigrep library as an exercise.

blocks.md: A last feature: an option for **case-insensitive** search, controlled by an **environment variable**. Users can set it once in their shell session and every search uses it. Again, the test comes first; there are now two tests, so give them distinct names:

blocks.explain: The `Duct tape.` line checks that the old search stays case-sensitive.
`to_lowercase` returns a new `String`, so `query` is now owned, and `contains` needs `&query`. The results are still the **original** lines, borrowed from `contents`, not the lowercased copies.

blocks.title: Reading the environment variable

blocks.code:
$ cargo run -- to poem.txt
Are you nobody, too?
How dreary to be somebody!

$ IGNORE_CASE=1 cargo run -- to poem.txt
Are you nobody, too?
How dreary to be somebody!
To tell your name the livelong day
To an admiring bog!
blocks.explain: In PowerShell, set it with `$Env:IGNORE_CASE=1; cargo run -- to poem.txt` and remove it with `Remove-Item Env:IGNORE_CASE`. Many tools accept both: an argument overrides the environment variable.

blocks.title: Standard output and standard error
blocks.md:
Terminals provide two output streams. **Standard output** (`stdout`) is for the program's results; **standard error** (`stderr`) is for error messages and diagnostics. Keeping them apart lets a user redirect results to a file while still seeing errors on screen. `println!` writes to stdout; **`eprintln!`** writes to stderr.

Right now minigrep prints its error messages with `println!`. See the problem:

blocks.code:
$ cargo run > output.txt
$ cat output.txt
Problem parsing arguments: not enough arguments
blocks.explain: `>` redirects stdout to a file. The user sees nothing on screen, and the error message ended up in the file where results belong.

blocks.code:
$ cargo run > output.txt
Problem parsing arguments: not enough arguments

$ cargo run -- to poem.txt > output.txt
$ cat output.txt
Are you nobody, too?
How dreary to be somebody!
blocks.explain: Errors on screen, results in the file: what users expect from command-line tools.

blocks.title: From Programming Rust: write to any Write
blocks.md: `println!` always goes to stdout. For testable output, write to anything that implements the `std::io::Write` trait: `fn run<W: Write>(config: &Config, out: &mut W)`. In `main` pass `&mut std::io::stdout()`; in tests pass a `Vec<u8>` and check its contents. `writeln!(out, "{line}")?` works like `println!` but returns a `Result`.

blocks.title: The minigrep library
blocks.goal: Write the whole tested library half of minigrep: Config::build with an option and environment variable, search, search_case_insensitive, and run writing to any Write.
blocks.behavior:
- `pub struct Config { pub query: String, pub file_path: String, pub ignore_case: bool }`.
- `pub fn build(args: &[String], ignore_case_env: bool) -> Result<Config, &'static str>`: `args[1]` and `args[2]` are query and path (fewer: `Err("not enough arguments")`). An optional `args[3]` may be `"-i"` (ignore case) or `"-s"` (case-sensitive, overriding the environment); anything else is `Err("unknown option")`. Without an option, `ignore_case` comes from `ignore_case_env`. (The real `main` passes `env::var("IGNORE_CASE").is_ok()`; passing it in keeps `build` testable.)
- `pub fn search<'a>(query: &str, contents: &'a str) -> Vec<&'a str>` and `pub fn search_case_insensitive<'a>(...)` as in the lessons.
- `pub fn run_on<W: std::io::Write>(config: &Config, contents: &str, out: &mut W) -> std::io::Result<usize>`: writes each matching line followed by `\n` and returns how many lines matched.
hints: Option parsing: `match args.get(3).map(|s| s.as_str()) { None => ignore_case_env, Some("-i") => true, Some("-s") => false, Some(_) => return Err("unknown option") }`.
`run_on`: choose the search function with `if config.ignore_case { ... } else { ... }`, then `writeln!(out, "{line}")?` for each result.
blocks.solution_explain: With this library, `main.rs` only has to collect the arguments, call `Config::build(&args, env::var("IGNORE_CASE").is_ok())`, read the file, and call `run_on(&config, &contents, &mut io::stdout())`, printing any error with `eprintln!`. Every decision is tested; only plumbing is left untested.

questions.q: What does `env::var("IGNORE_CASE").is_ok()` return when the variable is set to `0`?
questions.explanation: Only whether it is set matters in this design.

questions.q: Why should error messages go to stderr?
options: So results redirected with `>` to a file do not contain errors, and errors still reach the screen
questions.explanation: The two streams can be redirected separately.

questions.q: Which macro writes to standard error?
questions.explanation: (`dbg!` also writes to stderr, but it is for debugging.)

questions.q: In `search_case_insensitive`, what does the function return?
Why take `out: &mut W` with `W: Write` instead of calling `println!`?
options: Tests can pass a Vec<u8> and check exactly what was written

points: `env::var("NAME")` reads an environment variable; `is_ok()` checks whether it is set.
Lowercase both sides to search case-insensitively, but return the original lines.
stdout is for results, stderr for errors; use `eprintln!` for errors.
Writing to a generic `W: Write` makes output testable.

terms.def: A named value set in the shell that programs can read, like IGNORE_CASE.
The output stream for error messages, separate from standard output.
A macro like println! that writes to standard error.
std::io::Write, implemented by anything bytes can be written to: stdout, files, Vec<u8>.
